entities.name: gate block (城台)
entities.what: Massive brick-faced, battered gate platform carrying the tower; the road passes through it east-west. Two faces are painted: the south face, frontal, with dense horizontal brick courses, and the east (outer) face, receding up-right, its courses drawn as '///' hatching, with the passage's outer mouth in it. Its top is a terrace with a low balustrade on the south, west and east edges. Unguarded, no crenellations.
entities.vis: part: lower half hidden by trees (south face), the camel and the wall-foot crowd (east face)
entities.src: 余辉: 撤防的城门; sections.md §3 gate passage
entities.note: READING. Faces: S face from the SW arris (top 6478,821; visible down to 6430,1160, leans right going up: batter -0.13 px u per px v going down) to the SE arris (top 7068,821, runs down-right at +0.22 px u per px v, measured 7072,820 -> 7089,897). Terrace S edge = balustrade base v 820 (top rail v 763). E face: top edge = E balustrade base from the SE terrace corner (7068,821) to the NE terrace corner (7505,400), vector (437,-421). NE arris (line B) from (7510,397) down-right through (7700,935), slope +0.35 px u/px v. Two narrow vertical strips flank the passage on the E face: a dark strip 30-40 px wide from the balustrade (7152-7185, 690) to about (7290-7330, 1300) near the SE corner, and a lighter strip (band H) between line A (7440,473 -> 7570,880, slope +0.30) and line B near the NE corner; read as corner pilasters/piers (symmetric about the passage), not separate walls. No W or N face is visible (oblique shows S + E + top). HOW THE HIDDEN FOOT WAS ESTIMATED. The only drawn ground level on the block is the passage floor at the outer mouth (see S5.str.gate_passage: N jamb foot 7584,1290, S jamb foot 7442,1415). The E-face foot line was taken through those two points, parallel to the lintel (slope -0.88); se = its intersection with the SE arris, ne = with line B. sw = SW arris extended to the same v as se (S-face foot horizontal); nw = sw + (ne - se). So the footprint is est, conf low; the S and N piers come out symmetric (200 and 184 px of u from the passage), which supports the reading. Caveat at the NE corner: the recliner (seed S5.fig.wall_recliner, foot 7735,1098) and the man standing behind him sit 50-70 px west of this est foot line, so either the N pier is shallower / its foot steeper (a slope near the bridge's -1.6 would fit them), or they sit on a bank at the wall foot; ne is uncertain by about +-70 px. Heights (v px, base to top, include the batter set-back): se 770, ne 728. Batter on the E face: top set back about 170 px of u from the foot at the SE arris. SCALE CUES (px): S-face brick courses ~4.5 px apart; E-face courses ~9 px apart; terrace balustrade 57 px tall (763->820), posts ~65-70 px apart. DEPTH DIRECTION: E face lintel (136,-120), passage floor (142,-125), terrace E edge (437,-421), terrace W edge (6490,820)->(6587,717) = (97,-103); brick courses on the E face ~45 deg. So the gate block's oblique is about (1,-0.9..-1.0) per px u. Higher up the N-S lines flatten: podium E bracket band ~-0.7, hall E railing base -0.54, hall E eave -0.46 (checked by overlaying the three lines: the terrace line follows the E balustrade's base from the SE corner post to the NE corner). CONFLICTS: with this footprint the block's west foot is ~680 px of u east of the tax office's east end at the office's depth, although the painting puts the office right against the block's SW arris; and the hall above uses a much flatter oblique (see S5.str.gate_tower). The S5 frame (d = 28.75,-53.75) is steeper still.

entities.name: gate passage (门洞)
entities.what: Straight-lintel passage through the gate block, east-west. Only the outer (east) mouth is painted, as a tall opening in the battered east face; inside it the passage's north wall shows horizontal brick courses, a timber strip lines the south jamb, and a framed board with slats (the gate plaque, read by 余辉 as only '门') sits over the mouth. A Bactrian camel is walking out of the mouth, half outside.
entities.vis: part: outer mouth foot hidden by the camel and a seated man; inner (west) mouth not painted (hidden behind the block)
entities.src: sections.md §3: gate passage x ~7280-7450; camel caravan leaving
entities.note: se/ne = outer (east) mouth, S and N jamb feet; sw/nw = inner (west) mouth, est = outer mouth minus the block's foot width (868 px of u). Jamb lines: S jamb from the lintel (7282,773) through (7297,840), (7353,1093), (7430,1363): slope +0.22..0.235 px u/px v. N jamb from the lintel (7418,653) through (7467,840), (7533,1093): +0.26. Lintel/top from (7282,773) to (7418,653). Passage floor: the north wall's horizontal courses end at v ~1290 just inside the mouth (7450-7590), taken as the N jamb foot; S jamb foot = S jamb line meeting a foot line parallel to the lintel. The camel's hooves (~7450-7500, 1365-1385) stand between them. Timber strip (door lining or opened leaf) between the S jamb and a line ~35-50 px inside it (7332,840 -> 7370,1073; 7383-7393 at 840-1093). Plaque frame: slanted board with slats from (7270,700-790) to (7400-7410,590-640), in the plane of the E face, just above the lintel. SCALE CUES (px): mouth width along the face (142,-125) at the floor, (136,-120) at the lintel; opening height 642 (S jamb) and 637 (N jamb) px of v; camel in the mouth ~230 px from hooves to hump. The opening is a parallelogram, not a trapezoid (jambs ~parallel).

entities.name: tower podium and balcony (平座)
entities.what: Bracketed platform standing on the terrace and carrying the hall: a base course, a deep band of bracket sets (平座斗栱), and on top a balcony floor with a low railing running round the south and east sides; the upper stair rises to it from the terrace.
entities.vis: part: east side and north corners hidden behind the terrace balustrade and hall
entities.note: Front (S) foot on the terrace at v 717-720 from the SW corner (6583,719; it sits where the terrace W balustrade ends) to the SE corner (7152,720). Front: base course v 675-720, bracket band v 590-670, floor fascia v 560-590, balcony railing top v 532 / base v 557. E side: its foot is hidden behind the terrace's E balustrade. It must recede along the terrace edge (slope -0.96): a flatter line from the SE corner (7152,720) would pass outside the balustrade within ~50 px. ne/nw est = front corners + (318,-305), i.e. stopping ~35 px short of the terrace's NE corner (7505,400). The podium's E bracket band, drawn above the balustrade with figured panels, rises at ~-0.7 (7175,690)->(7320,605), (7300,580)->(7440,482). Support 'gate terrace' = top of S5.str.gate_block (not yet in the frame's supports). SCALE CUES (px): podium height from terrace to balcony floor ~159 px (719->560); balcony railing ~25-28 px. DEPTH DIRECTION: E bracket band ~-0.7, between the terrace edge (-0.96) below and the hall's E railing (-0.54) above: the drawn N-S lines get flatter with height.

entities.name: gate tower hall (城楼)
entities.what: The largest building in the scroll: a timber hall on the podium, 3 bays across its south end and 5 bays along its east side, with heavy bracket sets (intermediate sets between columns) and a hipped (庑殿) roof whose main ridge runs north-south, ending in 鸱吻 at both ends; the south end is a triangular hip. Lattice windows in the outer bays, a door in the middle bay of the south end where a lone figure stands at the head of the stair.
entities.vis: part: column feet hidden by the balcony railing; north and west sides hidden
entities.src: sections.md §3: 城上暮鼓; 名画记 five bays by three, hipped roof
entities.note: Columns: S end at u 6620, 6777, 6940, 7122 (bays 157/163/182 px); E side at ~7125, 7180, 7250, 7315, 7365, 7410 (5 bays, 47-70 px each) along the base line (7125,533)->(7412,378). Column feet hidden by the balcony railing, est at v 540 (S; the doorway floor, a little above the railing base v 557) and on the E base line (7125,540)->(7412,385). sw_top/se_top = column tops under the bracket band (v ~387); *_eave = the tile-end line at the same u (front eave v 276-280); ne_eave on the E eave line. Custom points (not straight above a base corner): ridge_s_end = S 鸱吻 base (ornament 24-88), straight above the middle of the S side (6872); ridge_n_end = N 鸱吻 (ornament 6-29), roughly above the middle of the N side (~7160); eave_corner_* = upturned eave corners (SE corner ornament hangs at 7260-7290, 307-333). Hips: SW (6868,65)->(6503,276), SE (6868,65)->(7245,280), NE (7121,25)->(7574,129). The main ridge (N-S) runs (6868,65)->(7121,25) = (253,-40), slope -0.16, far flatter than the E base (-0.54): the painter flattened the depth with height. So the 5-by-3 hall's long axis is N-S, along the wall, as a gate tower's should be; the '3 bays' face south toward the viewer. Drum: not identifiable; the doorway shows the standing figure (seed S5.fig.tower_watchman) and dark diagonal shapes behind him at 6855-6890, v 440-500 that might be the drum frame (very low conf). SCALE CUES (px): column height ~153 (387->540 est); door in the middle bay: frame 6790-6900, opening 6805-6890 (85 wide), top v 443, ~97 tall to the floor; doorway figure ~93 tall; balcony railing ~25-28; S-end bay widths 157-182. DEPTH DIRECTION: E side base / balcony railing (287,-155) = slope -0.54; E eave (329,-151) = -0.46; ridge (253,-40). Flatter than the gate block (-0.9..-1.0) and the bridge (-1.6).

entities.name: lower flight up the gate block (马道)
entities.what: Long straight flight with a plank railing on each side, laid against the gate block's south face and rising north from the street to a gap in the terrace balustrade (u ~6710-6855); its treads are drawn as evenly spaced horizontal lines, lighter than the brick face on either side. Empty of people.
entities.vis: part: everything below v ~1180 hidden by trees; foot not painted
entities.src: sections.md §3: inner ramp (马道), two flights (this is the lower; the upper is S5.str.tower_stair)
entities.note: Top end at the terrace edge between the rail-top posts (6710,755) and (6855,760); top tread at v ~822. W rail visible from (6710,755) to (6555,1180); E rail from (6855,760) through (6807,880) to ~(6690,1130): both slope -0.38 px u per px v going down. nw/ne = straight below the top end on the block's S-face foot line (v 1591, est). sw/se = where the rail lines reach the silk's bottom edge (v 1790): with the block's oblique the flight's foot would lie beyond the silk, so the true foot is NOT painted (trees and house S5.bld.house_6390 cover the lower part). Reading: a flight perpendicular to the S face (treads seen from above, rails = depth + rise), not a ramp along the face (a profile ramp would show a 30 deg sawtooth). Running N-S, it climbs to the terrace west of the earth-and-rock mound (S5.grd.rock_mound_7200), which is where a 马道 belongs; rail slope -0.38 with the block's oblique implies a steep (~50 deg) flight. SCALE CUES (px): tread lines ~10 px apart; width ~145 px at the top.

entities.name: moat bridge (平桥)
entities.what: Flat timber bridge carrying the main road east over the moat, as wide as the road. Each side has a plank railing: a handrail on capped posts with diagonal braces and five or six horizontal boards below; sightseers lean on the near (south) railing to watch the water and on the far (north) railing with their backs to us. The deck's south edge shows a plain fascia beam; timber trestle frames stand in the water under both ends.
entities.vis: part: east end behind willow branches and the covered cart; far railing behind the leaning crowd
entities.src: sections.md §3: 平桥; 桥头观水
entities.note: Deck level = road level at both ends (no rise drawn). Lines = railing feet on the deck edges. rail_near: boards start at 8236-8250, handrail 8277->9130 at v 1468-1477, deck-edge line v 1563-1572; fascia below to v 1590 (W) / 1600 (E). Near rail ends at the end post 9100-9110; the fascia continues to ~9190 under willow branches, so se is est. rail_far: tall W end post at 8500-8510 (capital v 1037-1047) beside a rack-like frame of tall posts and boards (8520-8590, up to v ~1000); handrail v 1072-1090 from 8587 to ~9340, where the big covered cart (9330-9750, S4 seam) hides it; lowest board v 1147-1166. ne est = se + the W end's depth offset (hidden by the covered cart). WHERE THE DECK MEETS THE ROAD: no abutment, ramp or step is drawn at either end; the deck is level with the road. W end = the line sw->nw (near rail's first board at 8236-8250 by the bush bank; far end post at 8505); E end = se->ne (near rail's end post 9105, fascia to ~9190 under the willow). The only supports drawn are the two timber trestle frames in the water (S5.str.bridge_trestle_w / _e); masonry abutments, if any, are hidden by the banks' bushes. bays: first 7 = near-rail post feet (8318...9105, ~132 px apart), last 5 = visible far-rail posts (end post 8505, then 8650, 8787, 9085, 9295; others hidden by people). sw_top = near handrail above sw (railing 95 px tall); nw_top = far handrail at the W end (~77-85 px tall; end-post cap at 1037). SCALE CUES (px): near railing 95 tall; far railing ~80-85 tall; post spacing ~132 (near) / ~140 (far); fascia 25-30 thick; rail watchers ~147 tall (seeds); the screen cart's wheel just NW of the W end ~82 px across (8302-8385, v 1200-1281); the big covered cart's wheel past the E end ~170 px (9464-9629, v 1221-1400). DEPTH DIRECTION: sw->nw (257,-410), slope -1.60; the far railing's E end runs ~300 px further east than the near one's, consistent with the same offset. Steeper than the gate block (-0.9..-1.0) and much steeper than the hall (-0.54).

Inside: edge_n = building fronts (depot floor ~885, tax-office column feet 920-935); edge_s = behind the roofs of the south-side houses (est, v ~1440); the street is ~500 px of v deep and the caravan walks in its southern half (v 1250-1400). Through the gate: the passage floor (S5.str.gate_passage, inner mouth est). Outside: edge_n = the wall foot and the line of tree bases (7880,1000; 8050-8120,1030; ~8330,1060) to the bridge's NW corner; edge_s = top of the bush/tree bank (7380,1440 -> 8240,1560). The open ground outside the gate is about as deep (v ~1050-1470) as the bridge deck (1155-1570). On the bridge: edges = the railing feet. Centre: inside drawn through the caravan's line, then the passage-mouth centres (outer mouth centre 7513,1352 = S5 datum), the bridge's end centres (8376,1360) and (9328,1370 est). The road continues east into S4.

entities.name: background path (top right)
entities.what: Path on the far ground at the top of the silk, behind the pines: a porter with a shoulder pole, a rider on a donkey and a walker go along it.
entities.vis: part: inferred from the figures' feet; no edges drawn
entities.note: Feet: porter ~(8910,107), donkey hooves (8936-8979,121), walker (8993-9007,136). Seems to lead east toward S5.bld.house_9300.

entities.name: moat water south of the bridge
entities.what: Open water under and in front of the moat bridge, left as plain silk without wave lines, between reed and bush banks; the trestle piles stand in it.
entities.vis: part: cut by the silk edge at v 1790
entities.note: Water = blank silk u ~8250-9260 below the deck fascia (v ~1590-1600) down to the silk edge, clear between the trestle frames at 8510-8975. shore_w = east limit of the reeds/bushes at the bottom-left (grass blades 8195-8400, v 1688-1770); shore_e = west limit of the grass tufts (8930-9050, v 1745-1790) and the willows of the east bank. Both shores are est: no shoreline is inked. South of the bridge a moat parallel to the wall would run down-left toward u ~7500-8200 at the silk edge; there the painting shows the bush bank (S5.grd.bush_bank_7800) and pines, so the water is only this patch under the bridge. bridge_edge = the deck's underside along the near side (where the water passes under the bridge).

entities.name: moat water north of the bridge
entities.what: Blank silk beyond the bridge's far railing, between the big tree at the bridge's north-west end and the willows and cart canopy at its north-east end; people lean on the far railing looking out over it, so it is read as the moat continuing north. No shore, ripples or boats are drawn.
entities.vis: part: only the bridge edge bounds it; tree crowns above
entities.note: Blank from the far railing (handrail v ~1075, foot ~1160) up to the tree crowns at v ~800 (u 8650-9200). MOAT COURSE: water shows only under/next to the bridge. A moat parallel to the wall (N-S) would run up-right from here (and down-left off the silk south of the bridge); up-right of this patch the painting shows big pines and willows (u 9100-9450, v 300-900) and, at the top, ground with a path, riders and a house (v 30-160) - no water. Between the gate and the bridge (u 7500-8240) the painting shows dry ground with people, trees and bushes, no moat.

entities.name: bush bank south of the road outside the gate
entities.what: Low bank thick with pines and bare bushes along the south side of the open ground outside the gate, running from the gate's south pier to the bridge's south-west corner, dropping toward the moat at its east end.
entities.vis: full
entities.note: Line = where the vegetation starts below the open road surface (no inked edge). Ground below it is foliage down to the silk edge; at 8150-8250 it becomes the moat's west bank.

entities.name: east bank of the moat
entities.what: Bank with a big willow and bushes at the bridge's south-east end, grass tufts at its foot by the water.
entities.vis: part: mostly hidden by willow branches
entities.note: Inferred from the willow's position and the grass tufts at 8930-9050, v 1745-1790; no edge inked.

entities.name: background ground with mounds (top left)
entities.what: Open far ground above the tax office roof: low earth mounds and ink-wash ground strokes with a few small animals and trees.
entities.vis: part: trees in front
entities.note: Wash strokes 6150-6350, v 175-230; a mound with a tree at (6220-6260, 140-180). Animals there (6280-6400, v 150-190) are for the tile agents.

entities.name: earth-and-rock mound at the gate block's south-east foot
entities.what: A mottled mound of earth and rock against the gate block's south face at its east end, running south past the silk's bottom edge: moss-dot texture, pale streaks and lumpy contours, with no brick courses, no crest line and no crenellations. Trees grow on it and round it: the knotted elm on its slope, the old multi-trunk tree at its east edge, the big bare elm at its west foot.
entities.vis: part: trunks and pine foliage cross it; its south end is beyond the silk
entities.note: Re-read in the loyalty pass from gridded crops (gen/map/S5/loyalty/mound_grid.jpg, z2_b.jpg); replaces S5.str.wing_south. Scholars read this mass as the slumped earthen city wall with trees (余辉 土墙杂树; Hansen: an "unguarded earthen wall... trees and brush growing at its base"); in either reading the painted form is a low mound about 4-5 m across that ends at the silk's edge, not a coursed wall running north-south. Painted edges: W (7030,1700), (7010,1790); E (7380,1700), (7400,1790). Upward the mottling narrows to u 7110-7260 at v ~1300, where it meets the block's face: read as the mound's crest against the face (nw_top/ne_top, about 3.8 m), low confidence. Its foot along the block is hidden (est on the block's S-face foot, v 1591); sw/se are where the edges reach the silk's bottom edge, so its true south end is not painted. North of the block (u 7500-8300, v 150-1200, gen/map/S5/loyalty/north_of_block.jpg) the strokes show only the big willow and the old bole, bare ground and the far shed: no wall.
